Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The failing test `testLang303()` attempts to serialize and then deserialize an instance of `FastDateFormat` obtained via `FastDateFormat.getInstance("yyyy/MM/dd")`. The error reported points out that the field `mRules` in `FastDateFormat` is not transient and also not serializable. Investigating the code, `mRules` is a private array of `Rule` objects. The `init()` method initializes this array by parsing the date format pattern into a list of rules and converting it into an array for faster processing.

Since `mRules` is neither marked transient nor guaranteed to be serializable (the `Rule` interface or its implementations do not appear to be serializable from the investigation), serialization will fail. The test serializes the `FastDateFormat` instance including the `mRules` array which cannot be reliably serialized since its components are not serializable. This leads to the test failure on deserialization.

The current bug report suggests two solutions: either make the `Rule` interface (and thus the objects in the `mRules` array) serializable, or mark `mRules` as transient and add logic upon deserialization to call `init()` again to reconstruct the reusable rules from the pattern.

In summary, the cause of the failure is the non-transient, non-serializable `mRules` array inside `FastDateFormat`. Serialization attempts to serialize `mRules` which fails because `Rule` implementations are not serializable. The test fails because deserialization fails due to this field. The best fix would be one of the two approaches mentioned, so that the serialized form does not include unserializable state or reconstructs it correctly afterward.

Recent bug reports retrieved are unrelated to serialization issues and do not provide additional hints related to this problem.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
